summary: I rechecked all 36 tricks across the 6 hands. Every lead and follow followed the rules, every follower was offered only legal cards, every trick went to the right seat, the dealer rotated 1-2-3-4-1-2 and the standings added up to the right draw between seats 2 and 3. The one gap is in the prompt: each private hand message still carried a 'Living seats: [1, 2, 3, 4].' line, which the DESIGN and R19 say to remove. Two other small wording problems in the rules brief do not change play.

findings.where: every hand start, all seats (e.g. hand 1, seat 2, first question)
findings.observed: Right after the private line 'Your hand: [...]; dealer seat 1; hand 1 of 6; points so far: ...' the player was shown 'Living seats: [1, 2, 3, 4].' This line is not in the transcript's [to [..]] messages, so it is added when the question is put together.
findings.expected: The DESIGN says to drop living-seats lines, and SPEC R19 says the hand message has 'no other lines'. No seat is ever eliminated in this game, so the line carries no information.
findings.fix: Don't print the living-seats line when the game has no elimination, or when the game file asks for it to be hidden.

findings.observed: 'Each round runs in this order: the match is set up → a new hand → the deal → ... → the hand is scored → the standings → after the last hand.' This puts the one-time match setup and the end-of-match step inside every round, and it makes one round look like one whole hand, when each hand actually has 6 tricks (6 engine rounds).
findings.expected: PROMPT: the order should show setup once, then for each hand the deal and 6 repeated tricks (lead, follower 1 to 3, decide, announce), then scoring and standings, and the end of the match only after hand 6.
findings.fix: Write the order with its loops: setup once; each hand = deal + 6 × (trick) + scoring + standings; ending after hand 6.

findings.observed: 'Final points: seat 1 1, seat 2 2, seat 3 2, seat 4 1. Draw among seats [2, 3].' The seat list is printed as a Python list.
findings.expected: The DESIGN's example wording is 'Draw among ...' written out in words. It is correct but reads a little rough.
findings.fix: Join the tied seats into words, e.g. 'Draw among seat 2 and seat 3'.

idea_alignment: This is still Agram: a 35-card deck with no ace of spades, must follow suit, off-suit cards never win, the trick winner leads, and only trick 6 counts. The only change is the one the DESIGN lists: a 6-hand match for 4 players with a rotating dealer and most hand wins taking the match. A dealt-in-batches order (R7) and a hand-1 dealer picked at random (R5) can't be checked from this transcript, and only the draw branch of R20 came up, not an outright winner.
